skill.name: ascii-visualizer
skill.description: Creates ASCII diagrams for architectures, workflows, plans, comparisons, progress summaries, and file structures.
skill.summary: Generate clear text diagrams for technical planning and documentation.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

content.value_statement: Complex plans and architectures can be hard to scan in plain text. This skill turns them into concise ASCII diagrams for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates boxed ASCII diagrams for components and relationships.
Builds file tree diagrams with short labels and status notes.
Shows workflows and data flows with arrows and stages.
Formats comparison views for options, metrics, and tradeoffs.
Creates progress summaries with text bars and status markers.
Uses reusable diagram patterns from the skill guide.
limitations: Produces text diagrams only, not rendered images or vector files.
Does not validate whether architecture details are technically correct.
Needs accurate user context for labels, counts, and relationships.
Not intended for code syntax highlighting or Markdown tables.

use_cases.title: Document System Architecture
use_cases.description: Turn service boundaries, folders, and data flows into a readable text diagram for design notes.

use_cases.title: Plan Implementation Work
use_cases.description: Show phases, dependencies, and validation steps as a compact workflow before a build starts.

use_cases.title: Explain Technical Changes
use_cases.description: Convert release updates or refactor summaries into diagrams that are easy to scan in chat.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple File Tree
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ASCII file tree for this project structure. Include short labels for the main folders: [paste structure].

prompt_templates.title: Diagram a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ASCII flow chart for this workflow. Show each step, decision point, and final output: [describe workflow].

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ASCII comparison for these options. Include strengths, risks, cost, and recommended choice: [describe options].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Layered Architecture Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a layered ASCII architecture diagram. Include components, data flow, ownership, risks, and rollout phases: [paste context].

output_examples.input: Show the architecture for a web app with routes, feature modules, shared UI, API clients, state, and types.
output_examples.output: A layered architecture diagram with each folder grouped by responsibility and connected to the main application flow.

output_examples.input: Compare the current workflow with a proposed workflow for review and deployment.
output_examples.output: A side-by-side text comparison with phase names, expected benefits, risks, and a short recommendation.

output_examples.input: Summarize implementation progress for four feature tabs in a dashboard.
output_examples.output: A progress summary with one row per tab, completion status, component counts, and validation notes.

best_practices: Provide the concept, components, and relationships before asking for a diagram.
Set a width limit when the diagram must fit chat, tickets, or documentation.
Ask for status, priority, or owner labels when they help readers scan faster.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for code syntax highlighting.
Do not ask it to invent architecture details that were not provided.
Do not request wide diagrams for narrow chat or mobile reading contexts.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates ASCII diagrams for architectures, workflows, comparisons, progress summaries, and file structures.

faq.question: Does it generate image files?
faq.answer: No. It creates plain text diagrams that work well in chat, tickets, and Markdown documents.

faq.question: Can it validate an architecture?
faq.answer: No. It can present architecture clearly, but users must provide accurate technical facts.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when a plan, workflow, hierarchy, or comparison would be clearer as a text diagram.

faq.question: Can it make file trees?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes file tree patterns with labels for folder purpose, status, and ownership.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
